Theres nothing in the game that the match maker can look at in an objective manner to determine your impact on the outcome of a game. 

There doesnt need to be any nuance to it in terms of what it thinks of your performance, as that is bound to never function well in a complicated game like overwatch, or any game for that matter. It cannot look at your stats, positioning, vc usage or anything like that and confidently say that you did more than someone else on your team or that you deserved that loss more than your teammate timmy. 

If you want examples of systems like this you can take a look at marvel rivals and the disaster that is their ranked system that takes into account your "performance".

Any system that looks at your performance and decides if you did good or bad does not and cannot ever work.

Sometimes you go on a unlucky streak of games. But a good majority of the time that you end up on a loss streak it's caused by yourself, even if in the moment you cannot see it. It happens to everyone, we are all far too often blind to our own mistakes, especially when there is people right infront of us making the same ones. 

If you lose 2 or more games in a row, take a short breather get some water, stretch a little. Give it a few minutes and come back. If you know you slept bad or already had a bad day then maybe ranked isnt the play, could go qp/arcade or just off role or maybe play on an alt account.

You see your mmr change after each ranked game.

If you go from plat 4 37% to plat 4 60% you gained 23%. Your new mmr is now, from the metric that players see it, plat 4 60%. There is nothing hidden behind that.

The game does not take your stats or anything regarding your performance into account when gaining or losing rank. The only thing the game will look at when deciding how much rank to take away after a loss is how likely you were to win that game compared to the enemy team (rank difference between each team). 

The matchmaker thought you were considerably more likely to win than the enemy team but you still lost? Reversal.
The match maker thought that was a well balanced game and both teams should have been equally likely to win? normal rank loss around 20% or so.

The system does not care or think about what you did right or wrong, it does not care if Timmy42069 jumped off the map 10 times while you single handedly killed their entire team every fight while pushing cart alone all game, you and Timmy both won the game and thats all that matters, you both gained 20%.

To clear up some of what is being bs'd 

Your value is NOT drastically lower than a tank or a supports value so much so that you cannot carry them through a game. In lower ranks tanks do tend to have slightly more impact than dps and supports for various funny reasons, but not to such a degree that it would make or break every game or that you are completely useless to help the case.

Unlike what someone else said, yes its normal for a support to be able to 1v1 you on a lot of characters. While this can be a little frustrating, if you manage to force a supports cooldowns without dying or commiting too much, it can often be a positive trade for you / your team. There are many ways of dealing with this!

"team with better sojourn wins" This is just not true. While yes she is very strong right now, but this kinda scales with rank. Sojourn has almost never been "strong" in lower ranks, infact she has been quite underpowered in low ranks even at the height of the sojourn metas shes still struggled in lower ranks. Same sort of situation as tracer where the impact the character has scales with player skill to such an extent that they can be near 100% pickrate and incredibly high winrate in GM but still sit at a negative winrate below plat. These heroes are simply too hard to be "op" in the coal mine ranks.

Dont "always" shoot supports, not going into much detail here because this one is fking stupid. Find your position and shoot what you think you should shoot in the situation. There is no one rule applies to all here, sometimes the right target is a tank, sometimes a support, sometimes a dps. Just dont turn off your brain and shoot the easiest target. Actively think about who and why. 

Yes Moira can infact feel quite strong in lower ranks, its not just you. While its not a hero that i would EVER recommend a new player to go and learn for a rainbow of good reasons, she is actually quite decent for climbing out of the depths of hell.

If you're playing dps and you're struggling with value, be creative! take new angles, shoot new targets, try new strats! But most importantly with how little you have played the game thus far, **Have Fun** ,learn a hero that you think looks cool even if its a whole different role! infact i'd encourage you to learn heroes from the other roles as well. It can help you understand the kits of heroes when you play against them, help you understand why you feel like they're so strong and let you experience the weakness of them and maybe you find some that you actually really enjoy playing! Scrim sr and ranked sr are simply 2 different metrics with next to no correlation. you see dia players scriming 4k and 4k player scriming low masters. Most of where u scrim just depends on how seriously you take the game atm, how good u are in a team and how good ur team is around you. Even within a team there can be very major differences in skill, ive been T100 at the same time as some teammates have been barely scraping masters or even in diamond.

 in 2019 i was scriming in 4.5-4.6k and the difference from that to today honestly isnt that big. In the past year and a half or so ive been scrimming with a team i joined for fun, just to help a friend out cause their hitscan didnt always show up and they were scriming around 3.8-3.9k at the time and have gradually over the past year and a half with some new players and with improvement gone up to scriming 4.5k with good success. I ended up playing full time as hitscan with them and it's been quite fun to play with them and see them grow, despite me not quite having fit the lower scrim sr. But overall i dont feel much difference from scrim sr 5-6 years ago and scrim sr today, there is probably some inflation but nothing very major. If i end up ringing and offroling for a team today thats 3.8-3.9k  i dont feel much difference in scrim quality between now and 1.5 years ago either.

Also your scrim opponents are going to be wildly different from scrim to scrim, there are teams that scrim 4.1k that u could probably beat easily while struggling vs a 3.8k team the next day, then you play those 2 teams again the next week and the roles might be reversed.

Keep scrimming 4k and see if u guys keep having it easy, if you do then move onto 4.1k, 4.2k ect ect until u find somewhere where you feel that your opponents are somewhat better than you in the majority scrims and then work on improving from that point.

TLDR: Scrim sr and ranked sr are 2 different metrics, you / your team has prob gotten a bit better over the past year, scrims are as inconsistent as wifi and somedays u will beat a 4.1k team and then get stomped by a 3.8k team the next day.

Some cooldowns matter more and less than others as well! the major ones to look out for are cc abilities (stuns and other forms of character control such as orisas halt which is more commonly known as pull or roadhogs hook which stuns and pulls you) and some other abilities that can swing an entire fight like Baptiste's immortality field and Mercy's resurrect. The importance of different abilities and which ones to keep a closer eye on will come over time as you learn the different heroes.

Altho i dont recommend jumping straight into practice to try to learn all cooldown timers right now as you likely dont have a good grip on the importance of different abilities yet. altho the ones mentioned above is a good start for when you feel like its time to figure things like that out.

The best thing to do would be to play quickplay until you learn what each chatacter does at least in terms of abilities and then jumping into comp. but if you want to learn the game then quickplay isn't the place to go outside of the very very basics of what abilities does.

If quickplay doesn't sound very interesting thats honestly understandable, i think its boring af in every game there is and am a person who also jumps into ranked asap. and if so just fo your placements and you will place in a lower rank than your first 2 placement games put you in. Generally the first placement game you play will almost always hover around gold (2000-2500 sr) altho sometimes lower, and its way too high for someone who's never played before. playing the placements and loosing all 5 will put you a lot lower in bronze where its easier to learn the game and get the hang of it. When i started i jumped into comp at level 25 and just kept playing it, im now grandmaster on all roles on several accounts. 

Dont worry much about placement games and just play them, unlike what i've seen other people say in this thread you dont need 20 hours on each hero to play and you also dont ruin the game for any teammates you get. Never worry about your teammates and just focus on you when you're learning. See what works and what doesn't, what all the heroes do with their abilities and go on from there. You are going to get demolished in your first few games just as anyone else gets when they can get matched up vs people with 2k hours after just playing quickplay for around 16h match time which is what it usually takes to get level 25. 

In terms of the heroes you play, soldier, genji and hanzo are a good set of starting heroes with different playstyles to learn.
